chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn together, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: 'The divorce of the child is valid/permissible when he reaches ten years of age.'
ai.seo_question: At what age is a child's divorce considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that a child's divorce is valid upon reaching ten years of age, reflecting the Shia juristic view of 'bulugh al-ta'qil' (age of discernment) in matters of personal status. It highlights the practical application of maturity thresholds in classical fiqh, distinguishing this specific ruling from the general age of puberty (bulugh) which may vary by individual development.
